title: Add transactional downgrade guard, backup/restore, and version-pinning to private-installer (Helm/Terraform)
author: Priya Nair
description:
This PR implements coordinated upgrade/rollback safety features for the private installer (Helm + Terraform) with three primary components: transactional schema migrations, backup/restore orchestration, and a downgrade guard driven by version-pinning. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private reported partial upgrades leaving mixed schema versions and KV/cached state incompatible with older releases. This change reduces blast radius for failed upgrades and provides an automated rollback path that verifies data integrity before downgrading.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add transactional migration orchestration: wrap Postgres migrations in a migration-controller that applies changes in a transactional/confirmable sequence and records migration batch metadata to the installer state. Supports 'prepare/commit/rollback' phases.
- Backup/restore integration: introduce pre-upgrade backup hooks and post-upgrade verification steps. Backups are uploaded to the configured storage backend (S3-compatible or local NFS) using the installer credentials. Restore is gated and will be triggered automatically when migrations fail verification.
- Downgrade guard & version-pinning: require that upgrade manifests include an explicit version_pin field for critical components (db-schema-version, runtime-kernel-version). Installer will prevent downgrade unless a restore/verify sequence succeeds or a force flag with manual approval is provided.
- Helm chart changes: new hooks and Job templates for pre-upgrade backup and post-upgrade verification; CRDs for MigrationBatch and BackupRecord to track progress.
- Terraform module updates: variables and outputs to surface backup retention, storage config, and migration controller settings.
- E2E and unit tests: add integration tests for successful upgrade, failed migration -> automatic restore, and blocked downgrade scenarios.

Notes:
- The description includes implementation and justification; detailed design doc linked in Linear (ENG-1942).
- This is backward compatible with existing installer configs; new settings are opt-in by default.

Risks / rollforward plan:
- Migration controller has feature flags and is disabled by default; early adopters can enable by setting enable_transactional_migrations=true.
- We validated against our QA cluster and ran a production-replay on staging that exercised large schemas.

Related: ENG-1942, ENG-1978, SUP-8421.

review_comments: Evan Chen: Can the migration-controller operate in a degraded mode if the cluster lacks Jobs permissions? We should fail fast and surface clear remediation steps.

Priya Nair: migration-controller now checks for RBAC and will abort with a human-readable error. Added installer docs section on required permissions and a preflight check. (see commit 'installer: add preflight rbacs check')
Maya Alvarez: We need to ensure backups are encrypted at rest. How is KMS integration handled?

Priya Nair: Backups use the configured storage backend, and we added optional KMS-encryption parameters in Terraform. Documented in variables.tf and README. Will follow up with a PR that adds HSM examples for on-prem customers.
Liam O'Connor: Tests look good; one flake in post-upgrade-verify on slow artifact downloads. Recommend increasing timeout and adding retry logic.
Priya Nair: Increased timeout and added exponential retry to the verify job. Reran tests and CI is green.

These features are opt-in and disabled by default. Refer to docs/private-installer/upgrade-rollback.md for configuration and migration steps.
